parole.significato: larva of a scarab beetle (family Scarabaeidae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Engerling, from Middle High German engerlinc, from Old High German engiring (10th c.), diminutive of angar (“large larva”) (compare modern dialectal German Anger, Inger), from Proto-Germanic *angaraz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂engʷʰ-ir-.

Borrowed from German geschwind (late 16th century), a prefixed variant of Middle High German swind, from Old High German *swind, from Proto-Germanic *swinþaz. Thence also English swith, Gothic 𐍃𐍅𐌹𐌽𐌸𐍃 (swinþs).

parole.significato: metal can, used mainly for coal
parole.testo: Of unknown origin. Possibly borrowed from the dialectal German Kietze (“carrying basket”), from Proto-Germanic *kitjō-. parole.significato: silenced, (made) unable to communicate one's thoughts
parole.testo: From mond + dood, a calque of German mundtot (“silenced”). The term was reinterpreted as meaning "dead in the mouth", but it is originally a legal term meaning “legally incapable”, with the component mund- from Old High German munt (“protection, guardianship”), from Proto-Germanic *mundō.
From Middle Dutch tzitteren (15th c.), from Early Modern German zittern, from Proto-Germanic *titrōną, whence also English teeter and (perhaps) dither.
